author: @jeremyfowers

evidence.api_compatibility: No API changes. The workflow change adds release-v* to the branches trigger list but those branches do not yet exist. tools/version.py gains a --release-branch flag via argparse but the existing internal callers (version.py invoked as a module) are unaffected. No breaking or changing API contracts.
evidence.documentation: docs/guide/install/docker.md is updated with a table describing the three rolling tags (latest, candidate, edge) and the immutable versioned tags. This is accurate and complete — the PR includes both the workflow change and the corresponding documentation update.
evidence.manual_release_testing: This is CI infrastructure and documentation only. No user-facing behavior changes, API endpoints, CLI commands, or shipped artifacts are introduced or altered. The Docker install docs add a table describing the candidate tag, but this is documentation of the existing workflow change, not a new user-facing feature. No manual release testing is required. Residual risk: when release-v* branches are first pushed, the candidate image publishing will activate for the first time; the merge-queue CI ran against main and confirmed the build workflow still passes with release-v* in the branch list.
evidence.post_approval_commits: One commit was added after superm1's approval: tools/version.py refactored to use argparse instead of argv scanning. The commit message explicitly says this is in response to review feedback. The diff is minimal (add import, add ArgumentParser, replace sys.argv check with args.release_branch). It does not alter behavior, risk profile, or API/CLI contract. Not problematic — it is a direct response to reviewer guidance.
evidence.review: superm1 approved with an empty body on 2026-09-14T19:51:50Z. superm1 is the maintainer with subject matter expertise in Docker and containers per docs/dev/contribute.md. The PR author notes they are no Docker expert, and superm1 is the appropriate SME to validate. An automated review from chatgpt-codex-connector[bot] flagged a potential race condition: concurrent release-v* branch pushes without a concurrency policy could leave the rolling candidate tag pointing at stale code. This was not addressed. The bot is not a human reviewer with subject matter expertise. A human reviewer should be aware of this edge case.
evidence.security: No credential handling, network calls, code execution paths, or permission broadening changes. The GitHub App push for the release branch creator workflow (mentioned in the PR title/body) requires release-admin permissions on the repo, which is appropriate. No security concerns.
evidence.tests: No unit tests for the workflow or version.py argparse change, which is appropriate: workflow files are integration-level constructs tested through CI runs, and argparse parsing is self-documenting and already covered by the existing call sites. All required CI checks passed (llama.cpp validate, stable-diffusion.cpp validate, vLLM validate, CodeQL, C++ unit tests, packaging builds). Many checks were skipped because they trigger only on tags or main — the workflow change adds release-v* but those branches do not exist yet. The checks that ran all succeeded.

subject: ci: publish release branch builds to the candidate Docker tag (#3581)
summary: Adds Docker candidate image publishing for release-v* branches, a scheduled workflow to create weekly release branches, and refactors tools/version.py to use argparse.
verdict_reason: Small, focused CI change with Docker/containers expertise on review, passing CI, and only a minor argparse refactor added after approval in direct response to feedback.
